what_its_for: Trospium is used to treat an overactive bladder. It helps reduce the sudden urge to urinate, frequent urination, and accidental urine leakage (urge incontinence). It works by relaxing the muscles of your bladder so you have better control over when you urinate.
how_to_take: Take trospium exactly as your doctor prescribed. Swallow the tablet or extended-release capsule whole — do not crush, chew, or break it. Take the regular tablet on an empty stomach, at least 1 hour before meals, or take it first thing in the morning before eating. The extended-release capsule (Sanctura XR) should be taken in the morning with water on an empty stomach. Drink a full glass of water with each dose. Do not take it with a high-fat meal, as this can reduce how well the medicine works.
dosing: The usual dose of the regular tablet is 20 mg twice a day (morning and evening). If you are 75 years or older, or have kidney problems, your doctor may lower your dose to 20 mg once a day at bedtime. The extended-release capsule is usually taken as 60 mg once daily in the morning. Always follow your doctor's specific instructions for your dose.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember — but only if it is still at least 1 hour before your next meal. If it is close to your next scheduled dose or mealtime, skip the missed dose and take your next dose at the regular time. Never take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one.
storage: Store trospium at room temperature, between 68°F and 77°F (20°C to 25°C). Keep it away from heat, moisture, and direct light. Do not store it in the bathroom. Keep this medicine out of reach of children and pets. Do not flush unused medicine down the toilet — ask your pharmacist about proper disposal.
what_to_avoid: Avoid drinking alcohol while taking trospium, especially with the regular tablets, as it can increase drowsiness and dizziness. Avoid driving, operating heavy machinery, or doing anything that requires you to be alert until you know how this medicine affects you. Avoid becoming overheated or dehydrated, especially during exercise or hot weather, because trospium reduces sweating, which can raise your body temperature. Avoid high-fat meals right before taking your dose, as they can make the medicine less effective.
when_to_call_doctor: Contact your doctor right away if you experience: inability to urinate or very little urination; severe stomach pain or bloating; fast or irregular heartbeat; confusion, hallucinations, or severe dizziness; signs of heat stroke such as hot dry skin, high fever, or not sweating in hot weather; blurred vision or eye pain; or any serious allergic reaction such as rash, swelling of the face or throat, or trouble breathing. Call your doctor if your bladder symptoms do not improve after a few weeks of treatment.
when_it_works: You may start to notice some improvement in your bladder symptoms within the first 1 to 2 weeks of taking trospium. However, it may take up to 4 to 6 weeks of regular use to get the full benefit. Continue taking it as prescribed even if you do not notice immediate results.
special_populations: Older adults (age 75 and older): You may be more sensitive to the side effects of trospium, especially confusion, dizziness, and constipation. Your doctor may prescribe a lower dose. Kidney problems: If you have moderate to severe kidney disease, your doctor will likely reduce your dose to once daily. Liver problems: Use with caution if you have severe liver disease; talk to your doctor. Pregnancy and breastfeeding: Tell your doctor if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding, as the safety of trospium in these situations has not been fully established.
